labels: Everything here is proposed (P): languages for the peoples of the roster of 24 October 2026 (docs/design/roster.md) that had none. Merge into languages.json: add families.delving, append the isolates to families.isolates.members, add the entries under languages, and drop "dwarvish" from reserved_languages.

delving.name: Delving family
delving.summary: The speech of the dwarves, reconstructed from the hold names of the West Lands, the North Lands and the Great Wall range. One living daughter, Dwarvish, whose holds understand each other; the old forms ended in -a and kept sr where Dwarvish has hr. Whether the Pack-Tongue of the dwarf goblins belongs here is unknown. Proposed.

reserved_lifted.reason: The owner placed the dwarves on 24 October 2026: the great ranges of the West Lands and the North Lands and the Great Wall range.

amendments.reason: Gives the owner's spelling Hirolon a Giants' Speech reading, hir "ring" + -olon (the -on of the land with a link o): the ring-land, so that it does not read as Mirolic (hirolon.md, note on the name).

dwarvish.name: Dwarvish
dwarvish.summary: The speech of the dwarf holds: heavy closed syllables that end in a consonant, the breathed hr, and long compounds that take back an old a where three consonants would meet. Every hold speaks it, in the western ranges, the High Mountains and the Great Wall range, so the name of a western hold and the name of a northern one are built from the same words. Men learn a few words at the gates; dwarves rarely teach more.

script.name: Hold-runes
script.feel: straight cuts on stone and on bronze tallies, read from the bottom up like a shaft; the clans keep their reckonings, their contracts and their grudges in them

sound.consonants: b d g k h m n r l s t v
sound.codas: m n r k d l nd rn rm rk lm sk st mb
sound.orthography: hr is one sound, a breathed r. Doubled consonants are held. There is no f, p, w, z, j or y.
rules: place names end in a consonant: -hrim -kerm -und -ost -ek
a lost a comes back as a link vowel where three consonants would meet

morphology.notes: The old final -a is lost at the end of a word but comes back as a link vowel inside a compound when three consonants would meet (brund + hrim gives Brundahrim, "mountain hall"). Plural by -um. The holds differ little: the western holds clip -und to -un in speech, the High Mountain hold draws its vowels out, Kunhrim keeps the old forms; names are written the same in every hold.

sound_laws: final -a lost in words of two or more syllables

house.notes: A dwarf names his line by a stone, a metal or the work of its founder: -ord for a line, -ast for the line that opened a delving, -erm for a line of fort-wardens.

patronymic.rule: None; at the gate a dwarf gives his line and his hold, never his father.

person.notes: A given name is used inside the clan; men at the gate hear the line and the hold.

established_names.name: Kunhrim
established_names.reading: Dwarvish kun "deep" + hrim "hall": the deep hall. The drawn label of the Great Wall range read as the dwarves' own name (proposed).

established_names.name: Lunhrim
established_names.reading: Dwarvish lun "high" + hrim "hall": the high hall, the drawn massif (proposed reading).

established_names.name: Brundahrim
established_names.reading: Dwarvish brund "mountain" + hrim "hall", with the link a: the mountain hall. The Gunwyn exonym Chalwe-Brenn is a calque (proposed).

established_names.name: Gromkerm
established_names.reading: Dwarvish grom "stone" + kerm "fort": the stone fort. The Gunwyn exonym Garth-Stenn is a calque (proposed).

established_names.name: Hrakkerm
established_names.reading: Dwarvish hrak "iron" + kerm "fort": the iron fort, seat of Kunhrim and of its Iron Charter (proposed; replaces the Aenoran-looking Kerdun).

established_names.name: Hrennost
established_names.reading: Dwarvish hrenn "fire" + -ost "hold": the fire-hold, deep hall of Brundahrim, where the western powder was first made (proposed).

established_names.name: Hrunost
established_names.reading: Dwarvish hrun "old" + -ost "hold": the old hold, deep hall of Gromkerm (proposed).

established_names.name: Ilmahrim
established_names.reading: Dwarvish ilm "white" + hrim "hall", with the link a: the white hall under the snows of the High Mountains, deep hall of Hrakbrund (proposed).

established_names.name: Hrakbrund
established_names.reading: Dwarvish hrak "iron" + brund "mountain": the iron mountain. The Leren exonym is Karundun, "mountain fort" (proposed).

gnomish.name: Gnomish
gnomish.summary: The quick, quiet speech of the gnome holts: short open words that end in o, i or et, held double consonants and almost no cluster at the start of a word. Gnomes speak it only among themselves; to outsiders they speak the Common Speech, and few outsiders ever hear either.

script.name: Pot-marks
script.feel: tiny scratches on the rims of the gold pots, one mark for each coin; the village king reads the tally

sound.consonants: b d g k l m n p r s t v
sound.orthography: Doubled consonants are held. A word almost never starts with two consonants. There is no h, w, z or f.
rules: no cluster at the start of a word

morphology.notes: Compounds are closed; a final vowel is dropped before a vowel. Plural by -n. A crowned gnome adds -illo, "golden", to his name.

patronymic.rule: None; a gnome is known by his village and, if crowned, by his pot.

person.notes: Every village has one king, who keeps the tally of the pots and crowns the gnome whose pot is full.

established_names.name: Olodor
established_names.reading: Gnomish olo "hidden" + dor "holt": the hidden holts. The gnome card's own name; the Aenoran chart form is Deodolor (proposed reading).

established_names.name: Tovodor
established_names.reading: Gnomish tovo "king" + dor "holt": the holt of the eldest village-king (proposed).

hearthspeech.name: Hearth-Speech
hearthspeech.summary: The home tongue of the small folk: soft, voiced and round, with doubled b, d, m and p in the middle of a word and endings in -um, -el, -ip and -o. Among men the small folk use Gunwyn and the names men give them; the Hearth-Speech is for the table, the field and the hearth-names they keep among themselves.

script.name: Door-marks
script.feel: carved signs over round doors and on the lids of leaf-boxes: a household sign, a field sign and a tally of the harvest

sound.consonants: b d g h l m n p r s t v w
sound.orthography: Doubled b, d, m and p are held in the middle of a word; ou is said as in "soup". There is no k, z, x or f.
rules: two or three syllables, never one

morphology.notes: Compounds are closed with a link e where consonants pile up. Plural by doubling the last syllable in speech (dobbum-bum), never in writing.

house.notes: A household name is the name of its door, its field or its hedge with -um or -el; families who keep the Watch's fords add -ip.

patronymic.rule: None; a household name says enough.

person.notes: Every child has a hearth-name, used at home, and a field-name, used in Gunwyn with strangers.

established_names.name: Dobbum
established_names.reading: Hearth-Speech dobb "vale" + -um "home": the home vale. Men of Gunwyn call it Dolw-Grewn, "the Green Vale" (former label Hky; proposed).

established_names.name: Luddum
established_names.reading: Hearth-Speech ludd "hall" + -um "home": the moot-hall where the Warden of the Fields sits (proposed).

pack_tongue.name: Pack-Tongue
pack_tongue.summary: The speech of the dwarf goblins: blunt, nasal words packed with st, sk and kn, endings in -om, -um, -ust and -ak, and many trade words taken from Leren on the road. Its kinship with Dwarvish or with Goblin Cant is unknown; the dwarf goblins do not say, and the words they share with both look like loans.

script.name: Knot-tallies
script.feel: knots on the pack-straps, one knot for each load carried and paid; a boss reads a strap like a ledger

sound.consonants: b d g k m n r s t l v
sound.codas: m n k r st sk
sound.orthography: st, sk and kn stand at both ends of a word. There is no e, h or p: a Leren e becomes i in loans.

morphology.notes: Compounds are closed and stress the first part. Plural by -ust. A loan from Leren keeps its ending -ur, which the dwarf goblins use for any boss's seat.

patronymic.rule: None; a dwarf goblin is known by his boss and his road.

person.notes: A boss takes the name of his cave with -ur when he takes the cave.

established_names.name: Mustnom
established_names.reading: Pack-Tongue must "hill" + nom "hall, warren": the hill warrens. The drawn label, kept (proposed reading).

established_names.name: Krakur
established_names.reading: Pack-Tongue krak "iron" + ur "a boss's seat" (a Leren loan): the iron seat, where the boss gives out the iron (proposed).

lowspeech.name: the Low Speech
lowspeech.summary: The low voices that the rangers hear in the Aenor Forest: the speech of the Baelim, slow and creaking, built of long vowels said in two beats (oa, ua) and soft endings in -orv, -oam and -uar. It has no hiss and no click. No man speaks it; a few rangers know a handful of words, and the Baelim answer men in the Common Speech, slowly.

script.name: Bark-rings
script.feel: no writing; a stand remembers by the rings it grows and the scars it keeps

sound.consonants: b d g m n r l v h k
sound.syllable: CVC, slow, one to three syllables
sound.codas: m n r l rv rm lb lm
sound.orthography: oa and ua are said slowly in two beats. There is no s, t or p: the voice has no hiss and no click.
rules: never a cluster at the start of a word

morphology.notes: A name is said slowly and grows by adding roots: a young stand has one root, an old one three. No plural; a stand is one and many.

patronymic.rule: None; a Baelen is named for its stand, and the stand for its oldest tree.

person.notes: The Eldest speaks for the stand at the moot; a moot can last a season.

established_names.name: Goamboarv
established_names.reading: Low Speech goam "great" + boarv "forest": the great forest, the own name of the Baelim for the Aenor Forest (proposed).

established_names.name: Graulvoa
established_names.reading: Low Speech graul "old" + voa "tree": the old tree, the oldest stand; Baeldran is the Aenoran calque (proposed).
